bib.title: The Upper Confidence Bound Algorithm: Asymptotic Optimality (Chapter 8, Bandit Algorithms)

question: Can UCB be made anytime and have a leading regret constant that matches the Lai-Robbins lower bound?
contributions: Algorithm 6: UCB with confidence level f(t)=1+t log^2 t, which is anytime (no horizon in the index)
Theorem 8.1: finite-time regret bound plus limsup R_n/log n <= sum_{i:Delta_i>0} 2/Delta_i
Lemma 8.2: bound on the number of times an index exceeds a threshold above the mean

limits: Only 1-subgaussian rewards; Gaussian case allows smaller f(t) (Notes 2).
Asymptotic constant is not indicative of practical performance: lower-order terms can dominate (Notes 3).
Optimality of constant 2/Delta_i is asserted via the lower bound deferred to Chapters 15/16; not proved here.
No simulations in the chapter; only exercise 8.4 asks the reader to simulate (n=1000, mu_1 in [-1,1]).
practices: Use f(t)=1+t log^2(t) in the UCB index so the algorithm is anytime and asymptotically optimal (Alg 6).
Prefer the eps-optimised bound (8.1) over the eps=Delta_i/2 form to get the correct leading constant (after Thm 8.1).
